variables.reason: The typed ledger defines Ra as the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations. The KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness explicitly defines 'arithmetic mean roughness' with symbols Ra / R_a and the textual definition 'Mean absolute deviation of surface height from its mean level', matching the ledger quantity-name and description. That record states its SI dimension is length (si_dimension: L), which supports the ledger's L exponent = 1 and implies the other base dimensions are zero. pq_mean_roughness_height is an independent KB record for mean/average roughness height that likewise has SI dimension length and corroborates the length dimension assignment. Both records directly apply to the same physical quantity named Ra in the original problem (surface roughness amplitude statistics), so the proposed exponent vector (I=0,J=0,L=1,M=0,N=0,T=0,Theta=0) is supported.

The ledger labels kt as the peak-to-valley height. The KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height gives the canonical definition 'mean peak-to-valley roughness height' (symbols including kt) and states the SI dimension is length (si_dimension: L) with unit m, directly matching the ledger physical definition. pq_mean_roughness_height additionally documents mean roughness quantities with length dimension and corroborates that any vertical height difference retains the dimension of length. Therefore the proposed SI exponents (L=1, others 0) are correct for kt.

The ledger defines k_rms as the root-mean-square height of surface deviations. KB record pq_rms_roughness_height explicitly names this quantity (symbols k_rms, krms) and defines it as the 'Root-mean-square fluctuation of surface height about its mean' with SI dimension length (si_dimension: L). pq_mean_roughness_height offers corroborating documentation that mean-related roughness-height statistics have length dimension. These records apply directly to k_rms as used in the original problem and support the exponent vector with L=1 and zeros elsewhere.

The ledger describes Sk as the skewness of roughness height fluctuations. KB record pq_height_skewness defines surface-height skewness (symbol Sk, S_k) as the 'Third standardized moment of the surface-height distribution' and explicitly records its SI dimension as dimensionless (si_dimension: 1). That record pertains to the exact statistical moment named Sk in the problem, so the ledger vector with all zero exponents (dimensionless) is supported.

The ledger lists Ku as the kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations. KB record pq_height_kurtosis defines surface-height kurtosis (symbols Ku, K_u) as the 'Fourth standardized moment of the surface-height distribution' and indicates it is dimensionless (si_dimension: 1). This record matches the ledger variable name and role and thereby supports the exponent vector with all zeros.

The ledger defines ES as the effective streamwise slope of the roughness. KB record pq_effective_surface_slope names 'effective surface slope' (symbols ES, E_x) and defines it as the mean absolute gradient of surface height in a horizontal direction; it explicitly notes that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and is therefore dimensionless (si_dimension: 1). This directly supports the ledger assignment of all zero exponents (dimensionless) for ES.

The ledger gives Po as surface porosity. KB record pq_porosity defines porosity (symbols Po, P_o, phi_p) as the fraction of void volume/area and records its SI dimension as dimensionless (si_dimension: 1). That record directly corresponds to the ledger's Po quantity used in the roughness parameterization, so the proposed exponent vector of all zeros is supported.
